claim: PSN-IRT, applied to 11 LLM benchmarks totaling 41,871 items, reveals significant and varied shortcomings in the measurement quality of current mainstream LLM benchmarks.
stance_target: aggregate benchmark scores hide measurement-quality problems that item-level psychometric analysis exposes
scope_conditions: 11 general LLM benchmarks, 41,871 items, AAAI-2026 Oral
quoted_support: Based on PSN-IRT, we conduct extensive analysis which reveals significant and varied shortcomings in the measurement quality of current benchmarks.

claim: Leveraging PSN-IRT item-quality estimates, smaller benchmarks can be constructed that maintain stronger alignment with human preference than the full original benchmark.
stance_target: IRT-based item selection produces more efficient and higher-fidelity evaluation sets
quoted_support: we demonstrate that leveraging PSN-IRT is able to construct smaller benchmarks while maintaining stronger alignment with human preference
